newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, hedge selling.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures stayed lower by the close on Wednesday, pounded by day-long hedge selling after an early move up proved short lived.
"Hedge selling and that's really about the only interesting thing," said one trader.
Benchmark January finished $17 lower at $1,430 a tonne, about the same as the pre-midday levels after gapping unchanged at the open. The contract had ranged between $1,420 and $1,456.

One trader said that pending fresh news, the contract could remain in the immediate $1,415 and $1,476 range. There were no fresh fundamental factors behind Wednesday's fall, just continuing concerns about a built-up in robusta supplies especially from Asia.
"There's no shortage of African robusta either," one physical trader said. "This is putting London under pressure but in New York, the situation is different."
The day's volume reached 5,845 lots. Traders said some 1,000 lots were Jan/March switches which were traded at between $50 and $60.

In options, traders noted 100 lots Jan/March call spread traded at $17. There was also a butterfly, one option strategy, involving selling January $1,400 puts two times and buying January $1,350 and $1,450 puts.
The market took note of overnight news of slightly lower Colombian 1996/97 harvest and the possible demise of the heavily-indebted National Coffee Fund.
But one trader said there was no immediate reaction.

The demise of the fund would in the longer-term put a downward pressure on prices but traders said the market was now more concerned with the tight nearby supply situation especially in the United States.
